tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to know...'), focuses on user intent (asking if a cluster is healthy, triage/report requests) rather than internals, explicitly lists trigger contexts (even when user doesn't say 'dashboard' or name a subsystem, 'is my cluster okay' questions, latency/throttling spikes), and clarifies scope boundary against a sibling skill. It is a dense but single-paragraph description appropriate for the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to know whether an Amazon EKS cluster is healthy right now, or asks you to assess, triage, or report on the state of an EKS cluster... even when they don't say \"dashboard\" or name a specific subsystem."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into project-specific EKS check IDs (CA/CP/NH series), tool names, and workflow steps without explaining general concepts like what Kubernetes or EKS is. It stays domain-specific throughout.
tests.evidence: Grade the CA-series from references/cluster-addon-health.md via use_aws (+ use_kubectl for CA9): cluster status + health.issues (CA1–CA2)...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body avoids embedding large reference tables; thresholds, queries, and remediation details are explicitly deferred to reference files. Conditional branches point to references rather than inlining detailed data.
tests.evidence: evaluate against [`references/thresholds.md`](references/thresholds.md)` and `[`references/queries.md`](references/queries.md)` rather than inlining thresholds/queries

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body, both within the workflow steps and the reference table at the bottom.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference file link is paired with a 'when' condition — e.g., when grading specific check series, or 'before fixing any verdict' — rather than generic 'see for details' phrasing.
tests.evidence: [`references/grading-guards.md`](references/grading-guards.md) | **Before fixing any CA/CP/CP-M/CPM/NH verdict** — the false-positive controls (FP1–FP12)...

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file links use relative paths in the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/consistency-sensitive operations (grading guards, read-only constraints, CP-M fallback order) are prescriptive with exact sequences, while findings analysis explicitly grants freedom ('reason from the observed evidence... using your own EKS knowledge; do not recite a canned definition').
tests.evidence: reason from the observed evidence (what it means, symptoms, ranked probable causes, cascade risk, confidence) using your own EKS knowledge; do not recite a canned definition

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The CP-M source fallback explicitly establishes a default order (CloudWatch → Prometheus/AMP → raw /metrics → N/A) rather than presenting options as equal.
tests.evidence: follow the source-fallback order in references/control-plane-health.md (CloudWatch → Prometheus/AMP if detected (mandatory) → raw API server /metrics via use_kubectl get --raw /metrics → N/A)

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable approach for assessing any EKS cluster's health (detect sources, grade series, validate, produce report), not a one-off instance task.
tests.evidence: Work through these steps in order — each depends on the ones before it... Step 1: Detect observability sources... Step 2: Grade cluster, version & add-on health

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: While there's no section literally named 'Gotchas', the grading-guards reference and false-positive controls (FP6, FP11) embedded in Step 3 serve this purpose directly, calling out non-obvious pitfalls like empty-result ≠ PASS and 429 spikes ≠ scale control plane.
tests.evidence: an empty query / no-datapoint result is *unknown*, never an automatic PASS (FP11); a 429 spike is not "scale the control plane" (FP6).

tests.evidence: Then write the artifact per [`references/report-format.md`](references/report-format.md): header, overall health, sources & coverage, Control Plane scorecard...
